material: Black cast PMMA rods, opposed flow
quote: While in microgravity, flame spread was observed at O2 concentrations as low as 17.5 percent, in normal gravity, flame spread was not observed below 19 percent.
differs_in: Flow: in orbit a low forced opposed flow; at 1g the flow induced by buoyancy, which NASA says is an order of magnitude greater (p. 57). Rod diameters: three in orbit, four at 1g. NASA's oxygen values in orbit are averaged over each test (p. 59).

material: PMMA film, 100 µm thick, 2 cm wide
quote: The average spread rate over the 100-µm-thick sample in the normal-gravity experiments is found to be 2.0 mm/s (see Figure 2.19(b)). Although the instantaneous spread rate fluctuates slightly, the average spread rate and the flame shape remain relatively steady throughout the experiment. The opposed flow being generated by buoyancy, a steady spread is expected. Any variation is probably due to surface irregularities and other random factors. In a microgravity environment, the opposed flow is much lower with experiments conducted mostly at very mild opposed-flow velocities. For the same fuel thickness, the highest spread rate obtained is about 2.2 mm/s
differs_in: Flow: at 1g, downward spread in the opposed flow buoyancy induces; in orbit, the highest rate over several mild forced opposed flows. The 1g value is an average; the 0g value is the highest and NASA says "about". O2 20.7 percent in both (p. 49). Test B3 is the orbit sample named in Figure 2.20 (p. 49).
